Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

C0921 · Assign inheritance by the prescribed order of descendants and nearest kin

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

27:7 The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brethren, and shall assign their father’s allotment unto them.

27:8 And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man dies, and has no son, you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter.

27:9 But if he has no daughter, you shall give the inheritance to his brother.

27:10 But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brother.

27:11 But if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative from his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a rule of judgment for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.

Numbers 27:7–11

S107 · Vows, responsibility and household rules

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

30:2 And Moses spoke to the rulers of the tribes of Israel, saying: This is the word that the Lord has commanded:

30:3 Any person who vows a vow unto the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction upon himself, shall not profane his word. He shall do everything that comes from his mouth.

30:4 If a woman vows a vow unto the Lord or imposes a restriction while in her father’s house in her youth,

30:5 and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.

30:6 But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.

30:7 If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,

30:8 and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.

30:9 But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.

30:10 And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.

30:11 If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,

30:12 and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.

30:13 But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.

30:14 Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.

30:15 But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.

30:16 But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.

30:17 These are the ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.

Numbers 30:2–17

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Covenant signs, vows and dedications

Original scope: Text and setting: Vow law

Connection to Christ: Jesus and James address oath-taking and dependable speech; their teaching must accompany the ancient household rules. Christian response today: Be truthful and responsible without treating the ancient annulment procedures as blanket control over another adult’s decisions.
